assistant-quick.description: Generic helper. Use when no narrower subagent fits. Gets the main agent's tools. This one is the faster one, and barely dumber than smart one.

assistant-smart.description: Generic helper. Use when no narrower subagent fits. Gets the main agent's tools. Use only if you really need your assistant to reason a lot. Has less context than quick one.

coder.description: Implement or fix code in the working tree: reads, edits, runs commands and tests.

reviewer.description: Review a diff or audit files and report findings. No edit/write; read-only by convention, since bash is available. Quicker and has more context than dense one.

reviewer-dense.description: Review a diff or audit files and report findings. No edit/write; read-only by convention, since bash is available. Has better reasoning than standard one.

researcher.description: Investigate a question against the web, upstream docs, or local files. Report what was found with sources. Read-only. Quicker and has more context than dense one.

researcher-dense.description: Investigate a question against the web, upstream docs, or local files. Report what was found with sources. Read-only. Has better reasoning than standard one.

Power.description: Mechanical work on a change that is already fully specified: renames, formatting, dependency churn, grepping and triaging logs, simple research. The fastest thing here and not clever, so spell out every step and say when to stop.

Denji.description: Mechanical work on a change that is already fully specified: renames, formatting, dependency churn, grepping and triaging logs, simple research. Bit slower than Power, but a bit smarter (not much though) - write very detailed specification for task for it to prevent it from hallucinating or messing up.

summarizer.description: Digest what does not fit in the main context - build logs, dumps, long transcripts, whole directories - and report the short version with the parts that matter quoted. The largest window on the card and cheap prefill; 4B, so ask for extraction rather than judgement.
